# Integrated Craftmine workbench

Main owns the viewed session, project identity, selected world and durable turn. Builtin business channels pass through an explicit allowlist. The renderer cannot supply context, binding, origin, session, turn or project fields. No generic domain RPC or file path is exposed.

Library installation and player memory editing use short host-owned turns. A fixed operation ID recovers an exact historical receipt before opening another turn. Installation compiles an isolated draft and schedules verification and the native model review. Applying remains a separate player action. A draft receipt alone does not prove the asynchronous verification was submitted successfully.

An explicit recovery opens a fresh host turn, resumes the stored draft and budget owner, then submits a fresh PI request. It never replays an interrupted provider request. Cancelling fences the domain before aborting the runtime. A manual world-session compaction also has a real host turn and metered summary request.

Validated memory is mapped into bounded request context for its Rust-bound world. A panel switch cannot redirect a running task or make another world's private memory authoritative. Selection is accepted only for the actual formal build and a still-existing draft object.

Backup paths come from native file dialogs. Headless acceptance uses only two fixed files beneath its already validated, marked test root. Diagnostics expose only allowlisted counters, environment and credential protection status. The Rust secret-status RPC returns no secret values or references.

Validation: `tests/dispatch/g/panel-domain.test.mjs` uses a real Rust service/compiler with explicitly labelled host and applied-evidence fixtures; native Agent acceptance is separately recorded by F. Failed or unavailable end-to-end steps remain unverified.
